text_en:
A rather indulgent breakfast sandwich, beloved in both Singapore and Malaysia.

Ingredients

Brown Kaya
Coconut milk (ideally 100% coconut) - 400ml
Eggs - 2 large
White sugar- 150g (split into 120g and 30g)
Pandan leaves (optional) - 3

Kaya toast
White sandwich bread - 4 slices
Kaya - 40g
Butter - 20g to 40g

Half-boiled eggs
Eggs - 2 
Light soy sauce - 10g
White pepper - A pinch

Salt

Kaya

In a pan, slowly reduce the coconut milk into coconut cream at medium-low heat, increasing the viscosity and fat percentage. Take 400ml down to 240ml. This should take 10 to 15 minutes. Don’t rush on high heat and don’t let the milk reach boiling, otherwise you risk splitting. Set aside.

In a bowl, whisk the eggs until fully combined, pass through a fine sieve, then combine well with 120g sugar until completely dissolved. Slowly heat in the bowl over simmering water while constantly stirring until slightly thickened and uniform. 10 to 15 minutes.

Add the coconut cream and knotted panda leaves (if using) and continue stirring and heating, don’t allow to boil. If you have a thermometer, you’re looking to increase the temperature of the mixture to 80°C (180°F) and then keep it between 80°C (180°F) and 90°C (195°F) until it thickens to the point it can coat a spoon like in the video. Around 20 to 30 minutes.

Separately, add 30g of sugar to a saucepan, spread it evenly across the pan. Heat slowly until completely caramelised without stirring. Be careful of burning, a few bubbles are fine like in the video but you want to be careful not to overdo it. Once liquid, pour into the kayak while stirring. It may solidify temporarily but if you keep stirring while hot, it will combine. Season with a small pinch of salt and set aside to cool.

Eggs

Boil some water, then add 2 eggs. Let them sit in the water undisturbed for 6.5 minutes, then remove to cool slightly. Crack open and spoon into a small bowl, season with soy sauce and white pepper.

Kaya toast (2 sandwiches)

Toast slices of white bread in butter, then remove the crusts, spread with kaya, add 2 slices of butter to each sandwich and season with salt if your butter is unsalted. Half each sandwich.

Kaya Toast & Onsen Eggs 🍳🇸🇬
This is how they have em in Singapore.
With eggs in the fridge, no man is poor!

Onsen Egg Hack (No Sous Vide Machine)
Ingredients:
* 2 eggs fridge cold
* 750ml boiling water
* Soy sauce
* Black pepper
* Spring onion, thinly sliced

Method:
1. Place 2 fridge cold eggs into a ceramic bowl.
2. Pour over 700ml of boiling water (this should fully cover the eggs).
3. Cover with a plate & leave for 18 minutes.
4. Crack into a bowl season with soy sauce, black pepper & spring onions.

Note: Results may vary depending on your egg size and bowl. 
You might need some trial & error to nail it, but this should give you a good starting point! 🫡

Kaya Toast
* Toast
* Kaya (kinda like a coconut jam,  they had it at Woolies & Coles)
* Cold salted butter

Spread the kaya jam onto the toast, add thick slabs of cold salted butter, cut into soldiers then dunk into those beautiful runny eggs.

Sweet, salty, buttery...

text_en: What seems to be missing from the criteria is whether the kaya is actually authentic. A lot of places make their own kaya, but others just use store-bought versions, which often have artificial flavouring. One of the featured stores is a good example — it was a bit funny that it got a five-star rating when the camera clearly showed cans of commercial cheap kaya being used. It’d be great to see a bit more attention paid to details like this in future episodes.
